metaData.title: Reachy Mini goes fully local
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This blog post provides a comprehensive, step-by-step guide to running a fully local, private voice conversation pipeline on the Reachy Mini robot using Hugging Face's speech-to-speech library and open-source models.
metaData.summary: The article details how to set up a fully local speech-to-speech pipeline for the Reachy Mini robot, eliminating the need for cloud servers and API keys. It introduces Hugging Face's `speech-to-speech` library, a cascaded pipeline (VAD → STT → LLM → TTS) that exposes a Realtime API-compatible WebSocket. The guide covers running the LLM locally with `llama.cpp` and Gemma 4, installing and configuring the speech-to-speech library, and connecting the robot. It then delves into customization, explaining the rationale for a local setup (privacy, cost, control) and offering opinionated defaults for VAD (Silero), STT (Parakeet-TDT), and TTS (Qwen3-TTS). The article extensively covers LLM options, including running models in-process with MLX or Transformers, or decoupling the brain via a Responses API with various backends like vLLM, Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, or OpenAI. It concludes with instructions for running the engine on a laptop while the app runs on the robot.

mainPoints.point: A fully local voice pipeline for Reachy Mini is achievable using open-source models and Hugging Face's speech-to-speech library.
mainPoints.explanation: The guide demonstrates a complete, private, and cost-free setup by running all components (VAD, STT, LLM, TTS) locally, removing reliance on cloud services.

mainPoints.point: The cascaded pipeline architecture offers flexibility and performance, allowing users to swap individual components.
mainPoints.explanation: The VAD → STT → LLM → TTS cascade is presented as the most flexible open-source option, enabling users to optimize for latency, quality, or language by replacing any stage with a preferred model.

mainPoints.point: Decoupling the LLM via a Responses API is the recommended approach to address the primary latency bottleneck.
mainPoints.explanation: Running the LLM in a separate process using the Responses API protocol allows for independent scaling and optimization, with support for various backends from local llama.cpp/vLLM to cloud-based providers like OpenAI.

mainPoints.point: The guide provides concrete, opinionated defaults for each pipeline stage to simplify setup.
mainPoints.explanation: It recommends specific models like Silero VAD, Parakeet-TDT STT, Qwen3-TTS, and Gemma 4 LLM, while emphasizing that these are starting points that can be swapped based on user needs.

keyQuotes: Audio never leaves your network, the entire pipeline runs on hardware you control.
Cascades are the most flexible option in the open-source landscape today, and with the right pieces they're also the fastest.
The main bottleneck in the system is LLM inference latency. To address that, we support external inference engines exposed through the Responses API protocol.
Every stage of the pipeline is a trade-off: there are faster TTS models with lower quality, slower STT models with higher quality.

relatedArticles.title: Shipping a Trillion Parameters With a Hub Bucket: Delta Weight Sync in TRL
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces a novel delta weight synchronization method for asynchronous RL training that reduces per-step weight transfer from gigabytes to megabytes by exploiting the natural sparsity of bf16 weight updates, and implements it using Hugging Face Buckets for disaggregated training across arbitrary machines.

relatedArticles.title: Your Agent Can Now Train Models — Merve Noyan， Hugging Face
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Hugging Face's Merve Noyan walks through the full open agent ecosystem — from local coding agents and MCP integration to automated model fine-tuning via Skills and a real-world 30,000-paper OCR case study.

relatedArticles.title: Specialization Beats Scale: A Strategic Variable Most AI Procurement Decisions Overlook
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A 3-billion-parameter specialized model outperformed every commercial frontier API in a structured OCR benchmark at roughly fifty times lower cost, demonstrating that distributional alignment to the deployment task can be more decisive than parameter count.

relatedArticles.title: State of Open Source on Hugging Face: Spring 2026
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A comprehensive 2026 industry report by Hugging Face detailing the explosive growth of open-source AI, the rise of Chinese dominance, and the emergence of robotics as a primary sub-community.

relatedArticles.title: Any Custom Frontend with Gradio's Backend
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Hugging Face introduces `gradio.Server`, a new feature that allows developers to pair any custom frontend framework with Gradio's robust backend infrastructure, including queuing and ZeroGPU support.

relatedArticles.title: How NVIDIA AI-Q Reached \#1 on DeepResearch Bench I and II
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA AI-Q achieves state-of-the-art performance on deep research benchmarks through a modular multi-agent architecture, fine-tuned Nemotron-3 models, and specialized reliability middleware.

relatedArticles.title: Welcome Gemma 4: Frontier multimodal intelligence on device
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google DeepMind releases Gemma 4, a family of open, multimodal models (2.3B to 31B parameters) featuring architectural innovations like Per-Layer Embeddings and Shared KV Cache for efficient on-device and long-context performance.

relatedArticles.title: Building a Fast Multilingual OCR Model with Synthetic Data
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details NVIDIA's development of Nemotron OCR v2, a fast and accurate multilingual OCR model trained on a massive, open-source synthetic dataset of 12.2 million images, overcoming data scarcity through a scalable, language-agnostic rendering pipeline.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni: Long-Context Multimodal Intelligence for Documents， Audio and Video Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA introduces Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, a new open-weight omni-modal model that combines text, image, video, and audio understanding with a hybrid Mamba-Transformer-MoE backbone, achieving top accuracy on multiple multimodal leaderboards while delivering up to 9x higher throughput.

relatedArticles.title: Falcon Perception
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Falcon Perception is a 0.6B early-fusion Transformer that unifies vision and language in a single backbone for open-vocabulary grounding and segmentation, outperforming SAM 3 on complex compositional prompts.
